guidelines.detail: same as LRN-016 (The description gives a participant action as the process trigger, followed by another activity. The records show the start event and its outgoing flow are absent, as is the flow from the first action to the next activity. This is consistent with the learned guideline LRN-016; the closest documented guidance also covers stated process triggers (EVT-01). No extra_element records were provided.)

same as LRN-017 (The description supports the generated activity labels, but some include the activity’s purpose or alternative implementations. A concise label centered on the activity would prevent this kind of divergence. LRN-017 already states essentially the same guidance; this is a second request to propose the best supported guideline.)

same as LRN-005 (The missing-flow records show omitted transitions between activities and a synchronization point. This guideline is essentially the same as learned guideline LRN-005. I have not relied on the reference's follow-up branch, which conflicts with the described order.)

same as LRN-012 (The description supports the generated labels’ stated actions and outcome, while some matched reference labels are vaguer or narrower. This guideline is essentially the same as learned guideline LRN-012.)

same as LRN-017 (The description presents implementation as one activity with alternative forms, and the generated task already covers those forms; the reported missing action has a counterpart in that task. A concise activity label is the most relevant reusable guidance for the remaining label discrepancy, and it is essentially covered by learned guideline LRN-017.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description identifies work performed by a participant as the first step of the process: Model that work as an activity after a start event and before the subsequent activity; do not represent the work itself as the start event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description identifies an action performed by a participant as the event that initiates the process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states an activity together with criteria, optional supporting actions, or a later outcome associated with it: Label the BPMN task with a concise verb-object phrase for the activity itself. Keep associated criteria, alternatives, and subsequent outcomes out of the label unless they define the activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an activity together with its purpose, explanatory detail, or alternative ways of carrying it out

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description presents distinct activities in an ordered progression, including transitions into, through, or out of branches or synchronization points: Connect each consecutive activity with a sequence flow, preserving the stated transitions through branches and synchronization points.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description presents distinct activities in a particular order

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a specific activity or process-ending outcome: Label the corresponding BPMN activity or end event with a concise phrase that preserves the stated action or outcome; do not substitute a related action or add an unsupported one.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a specific activity or process-ending outcome

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description presents mutually exclusive alternatives or says an activity may or may not occur, and the paths later continue in common: Model the choice with an exclusive gateway, and reconnect the alternative paths with an exclusive merge before their shared continuation.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description presents several mutually exclusive ways to achieve an outcome and later continue along a shared path
